phoneme_profile.description: High central or retracted unrounded vowel; realization varies by speaker and context.
phoneme_profile.phonological_status: Analyses differ: /i/ and /ɨ/ may be separate phonemes or contextually conditioned allophones.
phoneme_profile.distribution_note: In native Russian vocabulary [ɨ] is strongly associated with non-palatalized consonant contexts.

historical_graphics.widely_accepted_origin: Cyrillic ligature combining yerъ (Ъ) and i (І or И), conventionally ЪІ / ЪИ.
historical_graphics.dating: Gradual development; no single invention year without a cited manuscript witness.
historical_graphics.caution: Graphic origin does not mean modern [ɨ] was mechanically created by combining the sounds of Ъ and І.

historical_phonology.yer_note: Old Church Slavonic ъ and ь represented reduced vowels; later outcomes depended on language, position and sound change.
historical_phonology.caution: Grapheme history and vowel history are related but distinct; ъ did not simply become [ɨ] in every context.

comparative_slavic.polish_y: Related high central/centralized vowel category, but realization and phonological pattern are not identical to Russian /ɨ/.
comparative_slavic.ukrainian_y: Ukrainian и has its own phonetic and phonological profile; it is not an exact equivalent of Russian ы.
comparative_slavic.rule: Shared transcription symbols do not establish identical pronunciation or direct letter-to-letter descent.

orthographic_history.civil_script: The Petrine civil-type reform of the early eighteenth century standardized printed letterforms; do not claim one decree created the exact modern glyph.
orthographic_history.1917_1918_reform: The reforms changed several orthographic conventions but did not abolish Ы.
orthographic_history.transliteration: Latin transliteration depends on the adopted standard; Y is not a universal phonetic equivalence.

interpretive_layer.title: Philosophy of the hard sign and the soft echo
interpretive_layer.thesis: The union of a hard-sign component and an i-component is a metaphor for graphic synthesis.
interpretive_layer.numerology: 16 + 10 = 26 is not an established etymological explanation; Ъ has no ordinary independent numeral value in the standard Cyrillic numeral system.
